forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Farmer response to high prices and agronomic interventions in West Africa will drive cocoa back down toward historical means.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: High retail prices are destroying confectionery demand. As high prices cure high prices, cocoa should revert toward $5,000 by spring.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Post-harvest months bring seasonal price troughs. As main crop deliveries arrive against weakening confection demand, prices often revisit major supports near $5,000.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Demand destruction among European processors and recovering West African main crops favor continued downward price correction below $5,000.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Mounting retail resistance and downstream volume declines accelerate correction toward historical equilibrium below $5,000/mt.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Weakening retail demand and gradual supply recovery point to rebuilding pipeline stocks, favoring downward balance sheet revisions toward $5,000/mt.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Consumer price resistance and slowing confectionery sales indicate demand destruction that could trigger an inventory destocking cycle.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Weakening retail chocolate demand combined with recovering West African mid-crop prospects makes a correction below $5,000/mt increasingly plausible.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Booms invariably collapse into a lower, flatter pricing regime. A slide below $5,000 is a standard mean-reversion trajectory for cocoa.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Demand destruction in confectionery and gradual harvest recovery could accelerate a price correction below $5,000 by spring 2027.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Demand destruction is setting in rapidly among major chocolate manufacturers, increasing the likelihood of sliding under $5,000.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Crowd consensus is 42%. Easing cocoa prices and demand headwinds suggest a very small tilt above the market line.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Broad commodity inflation and dollar trends limit downside room; falling back under $5,000 runs against the prevailing macro current.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: While high prices dampen demand, degraded soils and erratic rainfall prevent any sustained supply glut that would crush prices below $5,000.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Cocoa cannot sustainably drop below $5,000 while production fundamentals and aging acreage limit genuine harvest rebounds across West Africa.

forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Tree damage from climatic extremes prevents quick crop recovery. Expecting a slide below $5,000 under-prices the structural supply crisis.
